raw_response:
I'm 76 years old. I've farmed this same land for 50 years, since I was a young man. Never went to school — can't read — but I know every corner of my 12 mu. I have 6 people in my house. My grandson works in a factory in Shijiazhuang and sends money home, which helps. My son still lives here and helps during the busy times, especially wheat harvest and maize planting. That week between wheat harvest and maize planting is the hardest week of the year. We sleep maybe four hours a night.

I grow wheat and maize on 8 mu — that's my main crop, always has been. The other 4 mu I plant with cotton. My wife wants the cotton for our own quilts and clothes, and we sell the extra. It's a lot of work, especially the picking, but we're used to it.

This year? I'll do mostly what I did last year. Last year the wheat gave me about 400 jin per mu, which is okay. Not great, not bad. The maize did better — maybe 500 jin per mu. I don't like to change things. When you're my age, you see that changing too much usually causes trouble.

**My wheat** is already in the ground since last October. Right now it's greening up. I already put down base fertilizer before winter — about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu, same as always. Now at jointing time I need to topdress. I'll put about 15-20 jin of urea per mu. I know some young people say that's too much, but three years ago I tried less and my wheat turned yellow and thin. Never again. I'll irrigate three times — once now at jointing, once at heading in April, and once when the grain is filling in May. The electricity for the pump costs money, but without water there's no wheat. I spray for weeds once, and if I see aphids I'll spray again. I expect about 400-450 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

**For maize**, after we harvest wheat in early June, we have maybe five days to get the maize in the ground. My son will run the tractor to till. I buy hybrid seed from the supply shop — about 3-4 jin per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the row when planting, about 30-40 jin per mu. Then when the maize is knee-high, I topdress with urea, maybe another 15 jin per mu. I irrigate twice — once right after planting if the soil is dry, and once at tasseling in August. Maize usually doesn't need as much water as wheat. I expect 450-500 jin per mu.

**My cotton** goes in around late April. I use seed I saved from last year if it looks good, otherwise I buy new. Cotton is hard work. I fertilize twice — once at planting, once when it flowers. I irrigate twice. But the real work is spraying for insects. I spray maybe 5-6 times. Bollworms are the worst. I expect about 200-250 jin of lint per mu.

Money is always tight. Even though my grandson sends money, I don't like spending too much on inputs. If I buy too much fertilizer and then a drought comes, I've wasted everything. I'd rather apply a little extra than too little — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps. I mostly use family labor. My wife and I do the daily work. My son helps during wheat harvest and maize planting. I might hire one or two people for one day during wheat harvest if we're late and rain is coming, but I avoid it if I can.
